html:
In 1926 the new Republic of Turkey adopted a civil code taken almost word for word from the Swiss Civil Code of 1907. It came into force on 4 October 1926 and replaced the Islamic family law of the Ottoman Empire.

It was one of the sweeping reforms of Mustafa Kemal Atatürk after the founding of the republic in 1923. The justice minister, Mahmut Esat Bozkurt, had studied law in Switzerland. Turkey chose a whole foreign code, not a slow reform of sharia, to break with the old order in one step.

The code banned polygamy, made marriage a civil contract registered by the state, allowed women to ask for divorce, and gave daughters equal shares of inheritance. Women won the vote in national elections in 1934. In the countryside old customs and religious marriages lived on for a long time, but the code set Turkey apart from most Muslim majority states.
sum: In 1926 the new Republic of Turkey adopted a civil code taken almost word for word from the Swiss Civil Code of 1907. It came into force on 4 October 1926 and replaced the Islamic family law of the Ottoman Empire.
